summary: Mission Bay by Windsor is a 129-unit, 5-story apartment building at 360 Berry St, first leased under The Integral Group's "EVIVA" brand and completed in 2017 per DataSF Assessor records; GID Real Estate acquired the newly built property in August 2017, and it is now managed as Mission Bay by Windsor.

images.caption: USDA NAIP aerial orthophoto (2024 flight), cropped to the Mission Bay project area and its immediate surroundings
images.appeal_note: A straight-down orthophoto rather than an oblique aerial, but Oracle Park and Chase Center are both clearly recognizable landmarks in the frame, giving anyone who knows the city an immediate fix on the neighborhood.

images.credit: Firstcultural (Alfred Twu), aerial view from a departing flight, via Wikimedia Commons; CC0; downscaled to 1600 px

images.caption: Aerial view of Mission Bay, Oracle Park and the Caltrain/King Street area from a departing flight
images.appeal_note: Oracle Park's diamond and Chase Center's dome (with its own logo) are both clearly identifiable landmarks in one colorful frame -- reads far better at card size than the flatter government orthophoto.

open_questions: Precise month of completion/first occupancy in 2017 is not sourced beyond the bare Assessor year and RentCafe's 'Building constructed in 2017' listing text; a claim of an April 9, 2017 opening date was found only on an unrelated commercial blog (not a real-estate or news outlet) and was not used.

Trade press names The Integral Group as developer under its 'EVIVA' platform, and The Registry (news.theregistrysf.com) has an article announcing a groundbreaking ceremony for the project, but that article's date and details are behind a paywall and were not verified, so are not cited here.
Architect not confirmed from any source checked in this pass.
